name: @layernote/mcp

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the layernote projects this token reaches, newest activity first, with their kind (WEBSITE, FIGMA, STATIC_FILES for uploaded files) and how many open comments each has. A personal token reaches every project its owner reaches in one workspace; pass a project from here (name or id) as `project` to the other tools.

tools.name: list_feedback
tools.description: List the layernote project's comments, newest first: by default the open ones (status OPEN, IN_PROGRESS or IN_REVIEW). Each has its text, author, date, assignee, due date, board column, thread and where it is: on a live page (URL and CSS selectors) or on an uploaded file (file id and name, pin in percent, PDF page or video moment). Comparison-generated items carry an expected/actual analysis. Narrow it with the filters, e.g. one file, or `since` for what happened in a week (that includes resolved ones). Use get_feedback for one item with its screenshot, get_file to see a file with its pins.

file.description: Only comments on this uploaded file: its id from list_files, or part of its name (every file it matches)

since.description: Only items made, changed, resolved or replied to since then: an ISO date like 2026-10-08. Includes resolved items unless includeResolved is false

author.description: Only items written by this person (part of their name or email)

assignee.description: Only items assigned to this person (part of their name or email), or "none"

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: get_feedback
tools.description: Get a single feedback item by id, including its full comment thread, the screenshot of the spot it is about (the element on a live page, or the part of the file around the pin) and the pictures attached to it, returned inline as images. Other attachments are listed by name.

id.description: Feedback item id from list_feedback or get_file

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List the files uploaded to the layernote project (images, PDFs and videos) in the order of its Files sidebar: each file with its id, kind, page count or length, and how many open and total comments it has. A file with more than one version is listed once, at its latest version, with its `versions` (each with its own id and counts; comments stay on the version they were made on). Use get_file to look at a file with its open comments pinned on it, compare_versions to check an older version's comments against a newer one, and list_feedback with `file` for the comments themselves. On a Figma design project it lists the frames instead, in the order of its Frames sidebar: pictures of the design’s screens, marked `figma`, that get_file, add_comments and show_file take like files (a frame marked `rendering` has no picture yet). A website project has no files.

search.description: Only files whose name contains this text

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: get_file
tools.description: Show an uploaded file, or a Figma project’s frame, with its open comments pinned on it as numbered pins, returned inline as an image, with a legend that ties each number to the comment's id and first line. An image or a frame is shown whole; a PDF one page at a time (default: the first page with open comments); a video as a sheet of the frames its comments are on (up to nine, continue with `from`), or the single frame at `at`. The numbers only label this picture: refer to comments by their id in other tools. Rendering a PDF page or video frames can take a few seconds.

fileId.description: File id from list_files (or one of its versions), or target.picture.fileId of a comment

page.description: A PDF: the page to show, from 1

at.description: A video: show the single frame at this moment, in seconds

from.description: A video: continue the sheet from this second (the last call's view.nextFrom)

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: compare_versions
tools.description: For a file with more than one version (list_files shows a file's `versions`): shows the open comments of an older version each beside the same spot in a newer one, so you can tell which comments the newer version took care of. Each picture has the older version on the left with the comment's numbered pin, and the newer version on the right with a dashed ring where the pin was; the spot is the same page or video moment, at the same place in percent. By default the latest version against the one before it. Comments stay on the version they were made on: resolve the ones that are taken care of with resolve_feedback (only when the user asks), by their id. Six comments per call; continue with `offset`.

fileId.description: Any version of the file: an id from list_files or its versions

from.description: The older version, by number (default: the one before `to`)

to.description: The newer version, by number (default: the latest)

offset.description: Start at this comment (the last call's nextOffset)

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: show_file
tools.description: Open an uploaded file, or a Figma project’s frame, in an interactive viewer in the chat, for the user: the picture with its open comments as pins they can click to read, resolve or ask you about, a PDF page by page, a video moment by moment, and a switch between its versions. Use it when the user wants to see a file or go through its comments. To look at a file yourself, use get_file: this answer only names the comments. In a client that shows no MCP Apps, nothing opens.

fileId.description: File id from list_files (any version), or target.picture.fileId of a comment

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: file_picture
tools.description: Used by the file viewer that show_file opens: the picture of a file, a PDF page or a video frame without pins (the viewer draws its own). To look at a file yourself, use get_file.

at.description: A video: the moment, in seconds

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: resolve_feedback
tools.description: Mark a feedback item as resolved in layernote. Only call this once the point has actually been dealt with: in the code, the design or the file. If it will NOT be done (a false positive, intentional, out of scope), use wont_fix_feedback instead so the team sees the reason rather than a false "fixed".

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: verify_feedback
tools.description: Only for feedback on a live website page. Ask layernote to confirm a fix: it re-screenshots the live page, re-runs the design comparison, and auto-resolves the feedback item when the underlying difference is gone. Prefer this over resolve_feedback for comparison-generated items — it proves the fix instead of trusting it. The deployed page must include your change first. Takes up to ~30 seconds. Comments on uploaded files cannot be verified this way.

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: add_feedback_comment
tools.description: Add a reply to a feedback item's thread in layernote so the team can follow along: what was changed, why, a question for the reviewer, or that a fix is waiting on a deploy. The reply appears in the item's thread under the name of the person who created the token.

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: wont_fix_feedback
tools.description: Mark a feedback item as "won't fix" in layernote, with a mandatory reason that is posted to the item’s thread. Use this instead of resolve_feedback when it is deliberately not acted on: e.g. the item is a false positive, intentional, or out of scope. The team sees the item as dismissed with the explanation, not as fixed.

reason.description: Why this will not be fixed (shown to the team)

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: set_feedback_status
tools.description: Move a feedback item to another status on the project board. Statuses are the project's own board columns — list_feedback returns them under "workflow.statuses", and clients can rename columns or add custom ones (e.g. "Design Review"), so always use a name from that list. Built-in names like "In Progress" also work. For resolving prefer resolve_feedback (or verify_feedback on a website), and for dismissing use wont_fix_feedback: that also records why in the thread.

status.description: Target status: a column name from list_feedback's workflow.statuses

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: add_comments
tools.description: Place one or more comments on an uploaded file in layernote, or on a Figma project’s frame, each as a pin at a spot on the picture (in percent, 0,0 top left), on a PDF page or at a moment in a video. A frame takes no page or moment. They appear at once for everyone on the project, clients on a share link included, under the name of the person who created the token and marked "via Claude". Look at the file with get_file first to place the pins well. Put every comment for one file in one call: the team then gets one notification, not one per pin. Only place comments when the user asks for it.

xPercent.description: The pin, from the left edge, in percent of the width

yPercent.description: The pin, from the top edge, in percent of the height

at.description: A video: the moment, in seconds (required on a video)

duration.description: A video: how long the comment runs from at, in seconds

comments.description: The comments, up to 50 for one file

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: update_feedback
tools.description: Change who a feedback item is assigned to, its priority or its due date in layernote. The assignee is someone on the project (list_people shows who), by name or email; they get the usual notification. Use "none" to take an assignment, priority or due date away. For the status use set_feedback_status.

assignee.description: Name or email from list_people, or "none"

priority.description: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH or CRITICAL, or NONE

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: list_people
tools.description: The people who can work on the project's feedback, with their name, email and workspace role: who update_feedback can assign.

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Add an image (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF) or a PDF to a Static files project in layernote, as a new file or, with versionOf, as the next version of a file (the same kind of file). Give `url` for one link or `files` for up to 10, for example the exports of designs you just fixed in Figma: layernote fetches them itself. For a file the user has on their computer, give no link: an upload panel opens in the chat and the user drags the file into it. Tell them so; an image pasted in the chat itself can’t be passed on. Only upload when the user asks.

url.description: An https link to the image or PDF, for example an image link from the Figma connector. layernote fetches it

fileName.description: The name to give it. A new version without one keeps its file’s name

versionOf.description: A file id from list_files: the upload becomes that file’s next version

files.description: Several links at once, each with its own name and versionOf

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: add_attachment
tools.description: Attach an image (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF) or a PDF to a comment in layernote, for example a picture of how it looks after the fix. Give `url`, an https link layernote fetches itself (such as an image link from the Figma connector). For a file the user has on their computer, give no link: an upload panel opens in the chat and the user drags the file into it. Tell them so; an image pasted in the chat itself can’t be passed on. Only attach when the user asks.

url.description: An https link to the image or PDF. layernote fetches it

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: store_upload
tools.description: Used by the upload panel in the chat, not by you: it sends the file the user dropped in it, with the ticket upload_file or add_attachment gave it. To upload a file, call upload_file or add_attachment.

ticket.description: The ticket the upload panel got

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Make a new layernote project in the workspace this token is for: FIGMA for a Figma design (then bring its screens in with import_figma_frames), STATIC_FILES for pictures, PDFs and videos (then upload_file), or WEBSITE for a live site (give websiteUrl). It counts against the workspace’s plan like a project made in the app, and is the user’s, made in their name. Only create one when the user asks.

type.description: FIGMA: a Figma design. STATIC_FILES: uploaded files. WEBSITE: a live site

figmaFileUrl.description: For FIGMA: the Figma file to link, as Figma copies it

websiteUrl.description: For WEBSITE: the site’s address, e.g. https://example.com

tools.name: list_figma_frames
tools.description: List the screens (top-level frames) in a Figma file, with their size and whether the project already has them: new, imported, or changed in Figma since. layernote reads the file with the user’s own Figma connection in layernote, not with a Figma connector in this chat. The project must be a Figma design project. Use it to pick frames for import_figma_frames. A big file gives up to 200 at a time: narrow it with `search`.

fileUrl.description: The Figma file’s link, as Figma copies it (File, Copy link)

search.description: Only the frames whose name holds this, e.g. "checkout"

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: import_figma_frames
tools.description: Bring screens from a Figma file into a Figma design project, the way “Add your Figma design” in layernote does: each frame becomes a screen the team can comment on. Name the frames (by name or id from list_figma_frames, up to 50), or leave them out for the whole file. A named frame the project already has is brought up to date when Figma changed it, and keeps its comments. One Figma file per project. layernote uses the user’s own Figma connection in layernote; when it is missing, the answer says how the user connects it. The pictures appear a few seconds after. Only import when the user asks.

fileUrl.description: The Figma file’s link, as Figma copies it (File, Copy link)

frames.description: The frames to bring in, by name or Figma node id. Left out: every frame in the file

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

tools.name: share_project
tools.description: Give the project’s share link, to send to a client or anyone outside the team: they open the project without an account and comment (or, with access "view", only look). A project has one link: the first call makes it, later ones give the same link. `access` changes what guests may do for everyone on the link. A link the team paused or that expired stays closed; `reopen` opens it again, only when the user asks for that. Anyone with the link gets in, so only share when the user asks.

access.description: comment: guests can comment. view: they can only look. Left out: as it is (a new link lets them comment)

reopen.description: Open a paused or expired link again

project.description: The project, by name or id from list_projects. Only needed when the token reaches several projects

instructions:
layernote holds a team's review comments on a project: live websites, Figma designs or uploaded files, with comments pinned on them.

- This token reaches several projects. list_projects shows them; every other tool takes `project` (a name or id) to say which one. When the user does not say, ask, or pick the project that clearly fits.
- list_feedback gives the open comments with their thread, author, assignee and where they are. Filter it by file, status, author or assignee; `since` gives what happened in a period, resolved ones included.
- To review a file yourself: look at it with get_file, then place every comment for that file in one add_comments call (one notification for the team). Pins are in percent of the picture; on a PDF give the page, on a video the moment.
- list_files shows the uploaded files with how many open comments each has. get_file shows a file with its open comments as numbered pins: an image whole, a PDF page by page, a video as a sheet of the frames its comments are on (or the frame at `at`). Look at the file before describing what a comment is about.
- The numbers on a get_file picture only label that picture. Refer to comments by their id in the tools, and to the team by file name, page or video moment.
- A file can have versions: list_files shows a file once, at its latest version, with its `versions` when there is more than one. Comments stay on the version they were made on. compare_versions puts an older version's open comments beside the same spot in a newer one, to tell which ones the newer version took care of.
- show_file opens a file for the user in a viewer in the chat, with its comments as pins they can click. Use it when the user wants to see a file; use get_file to look at one yourself.
- upload_file adds an image or PDF as a new file, or with versionOf as a file's next version, from https links layernote fetches (for example image links from the Figma connector, up to 10 at once). Without a link it opens an upload panel in the chat for a file the user has: they drag it in from their computer, as an image pasted in the chat can't be passed on.
- On a Figma design project its frames are its files: list_files lists them (marked figma), get_file shows one with its open comments as numbered pins, add_comments places comments on one in percent of the frame, and show_file opens one for the user. To review a design yourself, look at the frame first, then place every comment for it in one add_comments call. A frame marked rendering has no picture yet: Figma sends it a few seconds after an import.
- add_attachment attaches an image or PDF to a comment, from a link or through the upload panel.
- To set a review up from Figma: create_project makes a FIGMA project, list_figma_frames shows a Figma file's screens, and import_figma_frames brings the chosen ones in. layernote reads Figma with the user's own Figma connection in layernote; if it isn't connected yet, the answer says how they connect it, a step only they can take.
- share_project gives the project's share link for a client or anyone outside the team: they open it without an account and comment, or only look with access "view". One link per project; a paused or expired one stays closed unless the user asks to reopen it.
- get_feedback gives one comment with its screenshot and attached pictures. update_feedback assigns it (list_people shows who) or sets its priority or due date.
- The writing tools (add_comments, add_feedback_comment, update_feedback, set_feedback_status, resolve_feedback, wont_fix_feedback) act in layernote under the name of the person who created the token, marked via Claude, and the team, clients on share links included, sees the result at once. upload_file, add_attachment, create_project, import_figma_frames and share_project act under that name too, without the via Claude mark. Only use them when the user asks for it.
- On a website, verify_feedback re-checks the live page after a deploy and resolves the comment when the problem is gone.
